summary: Sweeps cross-section primitives along backbone curves to build path-following ribbons, tubes, ropes, rails, and skinned surfaces.
common_gotchas: Reference aiming requires the third input point count to exactly match the backbone point count.
fast needs consistent topology and equal cross-section vertex counts.
skipcoin can silently ignore coincident path points.
scale, twist, and roll may come from point attributes with those names.
Pre-skinned point replacement can outperform recomputing Sweep/Skin every frame.
key_concepts: Sweep SOP sweeps one or more cross-section primitives along one or more backbone primitives.
Backbones must have at least two points, and XY-plane cross-sections are normally easiest to orient.
Point color and texture coordinates on the backbone are preserved.
Reference-point aiming requires third-input reference points to match the backbone point count exactly.
Skin output and Fast Sweep are topology-sensitive performance choices.
